title: Mind the Gap: An Empirical Study of Synchronization Gaps, Delays, and Missed Opportunities in Software Forks
abstract: arXiv:2608.15803v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Fork-based development enables parallel evolution of software, but unsynchronized contributions create persistent divergence: security patches, bug fixes, and quality improvements often fail to propagate across fork families, leaving downstream users exposed to known vulnerabilities or bugs and missing massive opportunities to improve the other repositories in the family. We present the first large-scale empirical study of fork synchronization, analyzing popular GitHub fork families with 3,820 actively maintained forks, and developed a monitoring platform to mine the valuable commits and promote their swift merging.   Our findings reveal a synchronization paradox: while 90% of submitted pull requests are merged, only 6.92% of fork commits ever appear in PRs, leaving massive fork development permanently unsynchronized across the families. Synchronization delay is pervasive and structurally uneven where fork propagation accounts for 72.9%

translated_title: 关注差距：软件分叉中同步差距、延迟与错失机会的实证研究
translated_abstract: 基于分叉的开发模式支持软件的并行演进，但未同步的贡献会导致持续的分歧：安全补丁、缺陷修复和质量改进往往无法在分叉家族中传播，使下游用户暴露于已知漏洞或缺陷之中，并错失改善家族内其他仓库的巨大机会。我们首次对分叉同步进行了大规模实证研究，分析了包含3,820个活跃维护分叉的流行GitHub分叉家族，并开发了一个监控平台来挖掘有价值的提交并促进其快速合并。我们的发现揭示了一个同步悖论：尽管90%的提交拉取请求被合并，但只有6.92%的分叉提交出现在拉取请求中，导致大量分叉开发在家族间永久不同步。同步延迟普遍存在且结构上不均衡，其中分叉传播占72.9%。
tldr: 本研究通过大规模实证分析发现，GitHub分叉家族中仅6.92%的分叉提交进入拉取请求，导致大量开发成果永久不同步，并提出了一个监控平台以促进有价值提交的快速合并。
en_tdlr: This study reveals through large-scale empirical analysis that only 6.92% of fork commits enter pull requests in GitHub fork families, causing massive development to remain permanently unsynchronized, and proposes a monitoring platform to promote swift merging of valuable commits.
